_about: Maize problems recognised by the VLM, named as in ICAR-IIMR publications. key_signs are short field-identification cues drawn from ICAR-IIMR bulletins (Maize Diseases and their Management 2024; Major Diseases of Maize 2018; Insect Pests of Maize 2024; FAW bulletins) and are used by the second-check vision model. Advice/chemicals are NOT stored here: they come from the verified MaizeGPT table pests_diseases.json. Distinguishing signs for confusable problems revised 20 Nov 2026 from ICAR-IIMR bulletins (Maize Diseases and their Management 2024; Maize Production System 2010; Krishi Chetna zinc article 2024) after the agronomists' field test.

problems.name: Maydis leaf blight (MLB)
problems.key_signs: Small oval to diamond-shaped tan lesions that elongate BETWEEN veins into short rectangular brown lesions (about 1-4 cm) with darker margins, many per leaf, merging into irregular patches. Unlike TLB: lesions short and rectangular, not long cigar shapes. Unlike grey leaf spot: tan-brown with darker borders, wider and not strictly straight-edged.

problems.name: Turcicum leaf blight (TLB)
problems.key_signs: Long (2.5-15 cm) elliptical, CIGAR-shaped grey-green to tan lesions, not limited by veins, starting on lower leaves in cool humid weather; few large lesions per leaf. Unlike MLB: much longer, spindle shaped, fewer lesions.

problems.name: Banded leaf and sheath blight (BLSB)
problems.key_signs: Large water-soaked, straw-coloured lesions on the lower LEAF SHEATHS with alternating dark-brown concentric BANDS, spreading upward to leaves, husks and cobs; small dark-brown sclerotia on affected sheaths; seen 40-50 days after sowing in humid weather. Unlike charcoal rot: lesions are on the outside of sheaths as bands, stalk pith not shredded.

problems.name: Charcoal rot (post-flowering stalk rot)
problems.key_signs: Appears after flowering under heat and drought: premature drying of upper leaves, lower stalk dry, hollow and easily crushed; when split, pith is SHREDDED with numerous minute BLACK specks (microsclerotia) giving a grey-black charcoal colour. Unlike bacterial stalk rot: dry, no slime or smell. Unlike Fusarium: black specks rather than pink colour.

problems.name: Fusarium stalk rot (post-flowering stalk rot)
problems.key_signs: After flowering: plants wilt with dull grey-green leaves; lower stalk turns straw coloured; when split, pith is soft and decayed with PINK to reddish-tan discoloration; no black specks. Unlike charcoal rot: pink/red pith, not black specks.

problems.name: Bacterial stalk rot
problems.key_signs: Water-soaked, soft, slimy rot of the basal internodes and leaf sheaths during hot humid/rainy weather, often before or around tasselling; stalk looks boiled or discoloured; strong foul fermenting smell; plants twist and topple at the 2nd-3rd internode while still green. Unlike charcoal rot: wet and soft (not dry and shredded), no black specks, appears before grain filling.

problems.name: Pythium stalk rot
problems.key_signs: Soft, water-soaked, collapsed first internode above soil, plants fall over but stay green for a while; no foul odour.

problems.name: Common rust
problems.key_signs: Raised, powdery, cinnamon-brown ELONGATED pustules scattered on BOTH leaf surfaces, turning darker later. Unlike polysora rust: darker, elongated, on both surfaces.

problems.name: Polysora (southern) rust
problems.key_signs: Small ROUND, bright ORANGE to light-brown pustules, densely scattered mainly on the UPPER leaf surface, in warm humid weather. Unlike common rust: smaller, rounder, lighter orange, mostly on the upper surface. Unlike leaf blights: raised powdery pustules, not flat lesions.

problems.name: Grey leaf spot
problems.key_signs: Narrow RECTANGULAR grey to tan lesions with sharp, straight edges, strictly bounded by the veins and running parallel to them (matchstick-like). Unlike MLB: grey, narrow and straight-edged, no dark margin.

problems.name: Downy mildew (sorghum / brown stripe / Rajasthan)
problems.key_signs: Narrow chlorotic or yellowish STRIPES 3-7 mm wide running the length of the leaf, bounded by veins, later turning reddish-purple (brown stripe DM); whole plants chlorotic, stunted, with narrow, stiff, erect leaves; white downy/cottony growth on BOTH leaf surfaces in early morning; malformed tassels. Unlike zinc deficiency: whole plant affected and stunted from the seedling stage, stripes run the full leaf length, downy growth present.

problems.name: Common smut
problems.key_signs: Swollen silvery-white galls on ears, tassels or stalks that burst to release black powdery spores.

problems.name: Head smut
problems.key_signs: Tassel and/or ear replaced by a mass of black spores with thread-like vascular strands; leafy proliferation of tassel.

problems.name: Ear/cob rot (Fusarium, Aspergillus)
problems.key_signs: Pink-white (Fusarium) or green-yellow powdery (Aspergillus, aflatoxin risk) mould on kernels, often starting at the tip or insect-damaged kernels.

problems.name: Curvularia leaf spot
problems.key_signs: Small round to oval spots with light centre and dark brown margin surrounded by a yellow halo.

problems.name: Phaeosphaeria leaf spot
problems.key_signs: Small round to oval pale-green to bleached spots with dark brown margins, scattered on leaves.

problems.name: Bacterial leaf streak
problems.key_signs: Narrow tan to brown streaks between the veins with WAVY, irregular margins and a yellow halo visible when the leaf is held against light. Unlike grey leaf spot: wavy (not straight) edges, translucent halo.

problems.name: Viral disease (mosaic / chlorotic stripe)
problems.key_signs: Mosaic or fine chlorotic streaks/stripes on young leaves, stunting; often linked to aphid or leafhopper vectors.

problems.name: Fall armyworm
problems.key_signs: Window-pane scraping on young leaves, ragged holes, wet sawdust-like frass in the whorl; larva with inverted-Y on head and four dark spots in a square on the 8th abdominal segment; egg masses covered with buff hairs.

problems.name: Spotted stem borer (Chilo partellus)
problems.key_signs: Rows of small shot holes on unfolding leaves, dead heart in young plants, tunnels in stalk with frass; larva creamy with dark spots in rows.

problems.name: Pink stem borer (Sesamia inferens)
problems.key_signs: Pinkish larva without spots tunnelling the stalk, oblong holes on leaves, dead heart; common in rabi maize.

problems.name: Shoot fly
problems.key_signs: Dead heart in seedlings (central shoot dries and pulls out easily, rotten smell at base) within the first month; no holes on leaves.

problems.name: Maize aphid
problems.key_signs: Colonies of small soft blue-green insects on tassel, whorl or leaf undersides, honeydew and sooty mould.

problems.name: Thrips
problems.key_signs: Silvery or whitish streaks and specks on leaves, curling, tiny slender insects in the whorl, mostly in dry weather.

problems.name: Termite
problems.key_signs: Wilting and lodging, roots and lower stalk eaten and filled with soil, white soft-bodied insects in tunnels; worse in dry sandy soils.

problems.name: Cob borer / earworm (Helicoverpa armigera)
problems.key_signs: Larva feeding on silk and kernels at the cob tip, frass inside husk; larva striped, variable colour.

problems.name: Other leaf-feeding caterpillars (armyworm, cutworm)
problems.key_signs: Leaves eaten from margins or seedlings cut at ground level; caterpillar without the fall armyworm head/abdomen markings.

problems.name: Nitrogen deficiency
problems.key_signs: Yellowing of OLDER (lower) leaves starting at the leaf TIP and moving down the midrib in a V-shape; whole plant pale and spindly. Unlike zinc deficiency: lower leaves affected first, V-shaped from the tip, not bands at the base of young leaves.

problems.name: Phosphorus deficiency
problems.key_signs: Purple to reddish-purple colour on leaves and stems of young plants, dark green older leaves, stunting.

problems.name: Potassium deficiency
problems.key_signs: Yellowing and scorching (browning) of the MARGINS of older leaves while the centre stays green; weak stalks.

problems.name: Zinc deficiency
problems.key_signs: Broad pale-yellow to white interveinal bands starting at the BASE of YOUNG leaves on either side of the midrib, while veins, midrib and margins stay green; short internodes give a bunched plant; no downy growth. Unlike downy mildew: bands are broad and start at the leaf base, leaves are not narrow and erect, no white cottony growth.

problems.name: Healthy maize (no visible problem)
problems.key_signs: Uniform green leaves without lesions, pustules, stripes, holes, insects or discoloration.
